descriptionChirho: Core Qal active sense: to physically seize, grasp, take hold of, or hold onto a person or object with the hand, covering all active inflections (perfect, imperfect, imperative, infinitive, participle); Arabic أَمْسَكَ (amsaka = grasp/hold) consistently distinguishes this from the figurative sense; Korean 잡다/붙잡다 (jabda/butjabda = grab/seize); Swahili kushika/kukamata (hold/catch).

Qal sense where an emotion, fear, or trembling is the subject that 'seizes' a person, i.e., overcomes or overwhelms them; Arabic consistently uses أَخَذَ (akhadha = take) or اسْتَوْلَى (istawla = overwhelm) rather than أَمْسَكَ, indicating a different semantic domain; Korean uses 사로잡다 (sarojabda = captivate/overcome) rather than simple 잡다; Swahili patterns include emotional noun + kushika constructions.

Qal passive participle sense: to be taken or selected (often for a purpose such as a lot or portion); Arabic يُؤْخَذُ / مَأْخُوذ (passive of akhadha = be taken); Korean 취해진 (chwihaejin = taken/selected); Swahili ilichukuliwa (was taken); Spanish 'tomado' (taken).

Nifal and Qal passive sense of being caught or trapped, as in a snare or thicket; Spanish 'trabado' (stuck), 'atrapados' (trapped); Korean 걸린 (geollin = caught/snagged); Swahili amenaswa/wanaonaswa (caught/ensnared); distinct from simple passive 'be taken' by the entrapment/entanglement nuance.

Nifal sense meaning to take possession or acquire property/land, a legal-territorial meaning distinct from physical grasping; Arabic تَمَلَّكُوا / اِمْتَلِكُوا / فَاقْتَنَوْا (possess/acquire, entirely different Arabic roots from أَمْسَكَ); Korean 소유하다 (soyuhada = own/possess); Swahili kumiliki (own/possess); Hindi संपत्ति अर्जित करो (acquire property).

Hofal causative-passive and related forms meaning to be fastened, attached, joined, or bolted together (of structural elements, curtains, gates); Arabic مُثَبَّتَةً (muthabbata = fastened/fixed) and مَعْقُودٌ (bound/knotted); Korean 붙은 (buteun = attached), 매여 있었다 (maeyeo isseotda = was tied), 잠그라 (jamgeura = lock); Hindi जुड़े हुए (joined), चिटकनी लगाएं (put a bolt); Swahili vimeungwa (joined), kuziimarisha (strengthen/secure).

Piel intensive sense meaning to cover or conceal, semantically distinct from all grasping senses; Korean 감추시는 자 (gamchusineun ja = one who conceals); Swahili anafunika (covers); Spanish 'Cubriendo' (covering); Hindi ढाँकने वाला (one who covers); the Piel binyan here produces a fundamentally different meaning from the Qal.
